agnostic_oa_stochastic_control_transport.interpretation: Grounded inference: the stochastic and deterministic problems can be viewed as the same endpoint-constrained control skeleton with one representation-changing component—the Brownian fluctuation—inserted or removed. In the Brownian/quadratic case, the cost is not merely an arbitrary penalty: it is the control effort compatible with the reference noise, so sending the noise scale to zero exposes deterministic dynamic transport while preserving the endpoint-law constraint and action-minimization viewpoint.
agnostic_oa_stochastic_control_transport.nonparaphrase_operation: Perform a noise-removal comparison: start from the endpoint-constrained law of a controlled semimartingale, scale only its Brownian term toward zero, and track which parts of the optimization survive (endpoint marginals, integrated control action, and path evolution) and which change (random fluctuations versus deterministic trajectories). Then perturb the action away from quadratic growth and identify the exact step whose transport-limit justification is no longer supplied. This turns the passage into a reusable test for whether a stochastic-to-deterministic analogy is structurally matched or only superficial.

agnostic_oa_unbounded_entropy_renormaliz.boundary_or_failure: Representation dependence: the construction requires a sigma-finite reference r, an admissible exponential weight with finite normalizer, and finite weight expectation under the candidate probability. The first variational identity is stated under absolute continuity with respect to r; the continuous-test-function identity and lower-semicontinuity claim additionally depend on a topological/Borel setting, the weighted class C_W(Y), and its associated weak topology. Outside these domain and topology conditions the excerpt does not establish the same conclusions.
agnostic_oa_unbounded_entropy_renormaliz.interpretation: Grounded inference: the auxiliary exponential tilt is a choice of finite probabilistic coordinate system for an unbounded reference, while subtracting the expected weight and log normalizer is the change-of-coordinate correction. Because those corrections cancel when the admissible weight changes, the resulting entropy is intrinsic even though each computable representative uses a chosen tilt. The variational form then reveals why convexity and lower semicontinuity can survive this renormalization: the same quantity is exposed as a supremum of affine functionals on the stated weighted domain.
